learning_objective: 🎯 Decode the physics of movement! Learn to calculate how fast things go, distinguish between distance and displacement, and read motion graphs like a pro.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Distance is the total path you actually walked (a scalar). Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance from your starting point to your ending point, including the direction (a vector). If you run in a circle and stop where you started, your distance is the circle's perimeter, but your displacement is ZERO!

Speed is how fast you are going ($v = d/t$). Velocity is speed WITH a specific direction (e.g., '60 km/h North'). If you drive 60 km/h in a circle, your speed is constant, but your velocity is constantly changing because your direction is changing!
Acceleration isn't just speeding up. It is ANY change in velocity over time. If you speed up, slow down (deceleration), or change direction, you are accelerating! Formula: $a = (v - u) / t$.

On a Distance-Time graph, a straight diagonal line means constant speed. A flat horizontal line means the object is stopped. On a Velocity-Time graph, the slope tells you the acceleration, and the area exactly under the line gives you the total distance traveled!

When an object moves in a circular path at a constant speed, its direction is changing at every single point. Therefore, it is in a constant state of acceleration, even though its speed isn't changing!

fun_activity.title: 📍 The Square Walk
fun_activity.instructions: Walk 4 steps forward, turn right. Walk 4 steps, turn right. Walk 4 steps, turn right. Walk 4 steps. You are back where you started! Your 'Distance' traveled is 16 steps. But your 'Displacement' is exactly 0 steps!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the three equations of motion: 1) $v = u + at$, 2) $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$, 3) $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$. These are guaranteed to be in numerical problems.
📌 Always check your units! If speed is in km/h and time is in seconds, you MUST convert km/h to m/s (multiply by 5/18) before calculating.
📌 Be ready to explain why uniform circular motion is considered 'accelerated motion' (because direction changes continuously).
quick_recap: ⭐ Scalar quantities only have magnitude (size). Vector quantities have both magnitude AND direction.
⭐ The odometer of a car measures Distance, while the speedometer measures Instantaneous Speed.
⭐ If a body travels equal distances in equal intervals of time, it is in Uniform Motion.
